final_proof:
Fix \(z\in\mathbb C\) and put \(q=z^2+1\). We use the multifunction notation in its usual set-valued sense: \(\arg(q)\) contains all arguments of \(q\), and \(\ln(a)\) contains all logarithms of \(a\). Thus an occurrence of either multifunction ranges over all its values. When \(q=0\), the polar square-root expression has the sole value \(0\), since \(\sqrt{|q|}=0\).

First observe that
\[
\left\{\sqrt{|q|}e^{i\theta/2}:\theta\in\arg(q)\right\}
 =\{s\in\mathbb C:s^2=q\}. \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, if \(\theta\) is an argument of \(q\), then \(q=|q|e^{i\theta}\), and therefore
\[
\left(\sqrt{|q|}e^{i\theta/2}\right)^2=q.
\]
Conversely, suppose \(s^2=q\). If \(q\ne0\), write \(s=|s|e^{i\phi}\). Taking moduli in \(s^2=q\) gives \(|s|=\sqrt{|q|}\), while
\[
q=s^2=|q|e^{2i\phi},
\]
so \(2\phi\in\arg(q)\) and \(s=\sqrt{|q|}e^{i(2\phi)/2}\). If \(q=0\), then \(s=0\), which is precisely the zero-case value above. This proves (1).

From the definition of the multivalued complex logarithm, for every \(a\ne0\),
\[
u\in\ln(a)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad e^u=a. \tag{2}
\]
Consequently, if \(u\in\ln(a)\) and \(k\in\mathbb Z\), then
\[
e^{u+2k\pi i}=e^u=a,
\]
so \(u+2k\pi i\in\ln(a)\). Conversely, taking \(k=0\) shows that explicitly adjoining all terms \(2k\pi i\) to all values of the multivalued logarithm does not enlarge its value set.

We now characterize Definition 1. Given \(w\in\mathbb C\), set \(y=e^w\), so \(y\ne0\). Using \(\sinh w=(e^w-e^{-w})/2\), we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sinh w=z
&\Longleftrightarrow y-y^{-1}=2z\\
&\Longleftrightarrow y^2-2zy-1=0\\
&\Longleftrightarrow (y-z)^2=z^2+1=q. \tag{3}
\end{aligned}
\]
By (1), the last condition holds exactly when there is a value
\[
s=\sqrt{|z^2+1|}\,e^{i\theta/2},
\qquad \theta\in\arg(z^2+1),
\]
such that \(y=z+s\). Notice that \(z+s\ne0\): otherwise \(s=-z\), and hence \(s^2=z^2\), contradicting \(s^2=z^2+1\). Thus (2) applies to \(z+s\). Since \(y=e^w\), equation (3) is therefore equivalent to
\[
w\in\ln(z+s)
\]
for some permitted value \(s\) of the polar square-root expression. By the observation following (2), this is equivalent to \(w\) being one of the values
\[
\ln\!\left(z+\sqrt{|z^2+1|}\,
 e^{(i/2)\arg(z^2+1)}\right)+2k\pi i,
\qquad k\in\mathbb Z,
\]
where all values of the displayed multifunctions are taken. These are exactly the values prescribed by Definition 2.

Hence, for every \(z\in\mathbb C\), the set in Definition 2 is precisely
\[
\{w\in\mathbb C:z=\sinh w\},
\]
which is the set in Definition 1. Therefore the two definitions are equivalent.
